Optional fallback for networks without SASL. SASL is preferred when available.

Comma-separated command names, such as REGAIN or GHOST,REGAIN.

New account: connect with Authentication set to None, register, and verify your email; then return to Network settings. Existing account: select SASL PLAIN. SASL username is your account name (main registered nick); Password is your account password.

OFTC does not support SASL. Register with NickServ after connecting, then return here and use None, NickServ password, and Nickname, then password. CertFP is available as an advanced option in the official guide.
EFnet has no network account or nickname registration. Use an available nickname and leave Authentication set to None with credential fields blank.

IRCnet nicknames are independent from accounts. Create a web SASL account and PLAIN credential, then select SASL PLAIN. SASL username is your web login ID, not your nickname; Password is the credential password.
DALnet does not support SASL. Connect with None, register your nickname, and confirm your email; then return here and use NickServ password with Nickname, then password.

New account: connect with Authentication set to None, register your nickname, and confirm your email; then return to Network settings. Existing account: select SASL PLAIN. SASL username is your registered nickname/account; Password is your NickServ password.

New account: connect with Authentication set to None, register your nickname, and verify it; then return to Network settings. Existing account: select SASL PLAIN. SASL username is your main NickServ account; Password is your account password.
IRCHighWay does not support SASL. Register your nickname after connecting, then return here and use None, NickServ password, and Password only.
QuakeNet Q accounts are not SASL or NickServ accounts. Leave motd Authentication set to None, register a Q account, then authenticate manually after connecting with the official /auth flow.

Undernet nicknames are not registered; a CService username is separate. Leave Authentication set to None. Optional Login on Connect goes in Server password using the official PASS form, such as +x! username password. This preset is unencrypted.

DCC file transfers and safety policy.
DCC file transfers connect directly to peers.
motd only supports DCC SEND and SSEND file transfer. DCC CHAT and SCHAT are intentionally unsupported. Plain SEND is not encrypted; SSEND is encrypted but peer identity is not verified.

Auto uses active receive and direct active send. Private, local, and LAN offers require Allow once. Proxied networks never bypass the proxy; direct outgoing SEND is unavailable there until reverse mode is configured.
File offers will appear here after someone sends one, or after you send a direct file from a query chat.

Try experimental features. Off by default and kept out of backups.
Experimental work in progress. Labs stay off until you switch them on here, and they are never enabled by restoring a backup.
Dock a small orb at the screen edge; press and hold it to fan out a radial menu of chat actions.
Edit the rings, slices, and actions the orb fans out.
Show the experimental agent harness in channels activated by an Agentwire v1 topic. Off by default.
Connect approved apps through a private IRCv3 stream. Provider accounts and messages stay disabled when this switch is off.

Not paired. Tap to review access.
Open account, room, encryption, and diagnostics settings.
End-to-end encryption terminates in companion provider. Decrypted messages cross private Android IPC and are stored in motd history like IRC messages.
Sending blocked by provider security policy
Companion bridges disabled in Settings › Labs
Choose contact or room in provider
Merge every channel and DM into one stream, opened from the drawer or the chat list. Off by default.
Termbin sends text without encryption to a public service. Never upload passwords or private information.
Custom endpoints may allow uploads up to 512 MiB.
Enter a valid HTTPS URL without credentials.
Configure the Custom HTTPS URL in Settings › Uploads before uploading.
Ask the service not to list the upload publicly.
Maximum lifetime, such as 7 days; leave blank for its default.
The link is removed automatically after this duration.
Uguu uploads are public to anyone with the link and expire after 3 hours.
paste.c-net.org uses an unguessable link and supports deletion. Retention resets to 180 days whenever the file is accessed.
Catbox uploads are long-lived, cannot be deleted anonymously, and may remain until 2 years without access.
x0.at uploads are public to anyone with the link, cannot be deleted, and expire after 3 to 100 days depending on file size (larger files expire sooner).
Uses the file host advertised by the active IRC network. Uploads only work in connected chats whose bouncer exposes a Soju file host.

Optional. Tunnels IRC over a WebSocket (e.g. wss://bnc.example.com:443/) to look like ordinary HTTPS and bypass networks that block IRC. Requires a WebSocket listener on your soju server. Leave blank for a normal TCP/TLS connection.
Route this network through a proxy to bypass censorship. Opt-in and may add latency. The strongest options (Tor .onion bouncer, VLESS+REALITY) require setup on your own soju server.
Sets a SOCKS5 proxy at 127.0.0.1:9050. Requires Orbot running on this device.
Paste the VLESS + REALITY share link for this network. motd starts its embedded tunnel and keeps the loopback proxy private.
DNS is resolved remotely through the proxy (no leak; .onion works).
